title: Preamble — Constitutional ideals and popular authority
summary: Trace popular sovereignty, justice, liberty, equality and republican constitutional aims from December 1946 into the later constitutional family.

title: Article 1 family — India, the Union and its territories
summary: Trace how the political community, Indian States representation and Union-level constitutional machinery develop before the final territorial provision.

title: Article 14 family — Equality
summary: Trace equality from the Objectives Resolution through representation disputes into the April 1947 rights-drafting phase.

title: Article 16 family — Public employment
summary: The 30 April 1947 debate tests how equality in public employment can coexist with corrective measures for under-represented communities.

title: Article 17 family — Untouchability
summary: Trace how Scheduled Caste claims and the April rights debate make untouchability and caste hierarchy a distinct constitutional problem.

title: Article 19 family — Freedoms and restrictions
summary: Speech, association, movement and occupation are tested against public order, emergency, morality and legitimate regulation.

title: Articles 23–24 family — Exploitation
summary: The 1 May debate exposes drafting tensions between banning forced labour, preserving compulsory public service and protecting children.

title: Articles 25–28 family — Freedom of religion
summary: Religious liberty is tested against coercion, conversion, minors, family authority, social reform and State regulation.

title: Articles 29–30 family — Cultural and educational rights
summary: Trace minority protection from general safeguards into language, culture and educational-institution questions.

title: Article 32 family — Constitutional remedies
summary: The April rights debate asks which guarantees are judicially enforceable and whether ordinary citizens can realistically use constitutional remedies.

title: Part IV family — Directive Principles
summary: Trace the early divide between judicially enforceable rights and social-economic goals that guide the State without the same immediate court remedy.
